citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit
explanation: Fisher expressly overrules Gollehon's two-step money-mandating test, but the footnote states that section was considered and decided by the full Federal Circuit en banc (citing South Corp.); bench limb fails.

citing_name: George v. Hercules Real Estate Services, Inc.
explanation: Division 2 disapproves/overrules the quiet-enjoyment line including Albert Properties, but all fifteen Georgia Court of Appeals judges participated (whole court), so it was not a panel decision; bench limb fails.

citing_name: Frontera Resources Azerbaijan Corp. v. State Oil Co.
citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit
cited_name: Texas Trading & Milling Corp. v. Federal Republic of Nigeria
explanation: Three-judge panel overruled Texas Trading, but relied on intervening Supreme Court doubt (Weltover) and circulated the opinion to all active judges without objection (mini-en banc); recognised exception present.

cited_name: Hillman v. Federal National Mortgage Ass'n
explanation: Fourth DCA panel receded from Hillman, but justified it by conflict with its own earlier Harrell decision and Florida Supreme Court practice/rule (Adams v. Powers, Rule 2.040); recognised grounds given. En banc rule 9.331 existed (own knowledge).

El Paso panel overruled its own Daylin, but because Daylin could not be reconciled with earlier binding Texas Supreme Court strict-compliance authority (McKanna, Uvalde) and its own earlier Fleming; contrary-to-earlier-precedent exception stated.
Second DCA receded from Allen, but eleven judges participated (en banc court) and the opinion relied on the intervening Florida Supreme Court decision in Burdick; bench and exception limbs fail.

citing_name: Narragansett Indian Tribe v. Rhode Island
citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the First Circuit
cited_name: Aroostook Band of Micmacs v. Ryan
explanation: First Circuit expressly overruled Aroostook's sovereignty/sovereign-immunity distinction, but did so in an opinion marked OPINION EN BANC by six judges; not a panel decision, so bench limb fails.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit
explanation: Tenth Circuit panel expressly overruled Robison on the State's need to cross-appeal a procedural-bar ruling, but states it submitted the determination to the entire en banc court, which agreed; full-court approval is a recognised ground, so limb 3 fails.

citing_name: Dallas Sales Co. v. Carlisle Silver Co.
cited_name: National Loan Investors, L.P. v. Taylor
explanation: Waco court expressly overruled its own National Loan Investors on which judicial-estoppel law applies, giving no panel-exception ground; but from my knowledge the Waco court had only three justices, so Gray, Vance and Reyna were the whole court, not a panel.

cited_name: Wagstaff v. North British & Mercantile Ins. Co.
explanation: Eastland Court of Civil Appeals overruled a contrary indication in its own Wagstaff, relying on the earlier Supreme Court-approved Adams decision; from my knowledge 1939 civil appeals courts were three-justice courts sitting as a whole with no en banc procedure, so limbs 2-4 fail.

Corpus Christi court overruled Nunez and its other De Garmo sufficiency-waiver decisions, but did so in an opinion expressly issued en banc under Tex.R.App.P. 49.7 after withdrawing the panel opinion; the bench limb fails.

San Antonio court expressly overruled Seiler's holding that filing a condemnation petition in the wrong place is jurisdictional, but the judges line lists seven justices sitting, which from my knowledge is the full court sitting en banc; the bench limb fails.

citing_name: Cold War Museum, Inc. v. Cold War Air Museum, Inc.
citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit
cited_name: Brunswick Corp. v. British Seagull Ltd.
explanation: Federal Circuit panel overruled the TTAB's British Seagull decision as contrary to 37 C.F.R. 2.122(b), not its own Brunswick opinion; footnote says Brunswick affirmed only on functionality and never reached the evidentiary issue, so no same-court holding was departed from.

Alabama Court of Criminal Appeals overruled Beshears so far as guns alone were treated as exigent circumstances, but 'All the Judges concur' except one; from my knowledge that five-judge court sits as a whole, with no panel or prior-panel rule.
Fourth DCA expressly receded from its own Harvey holding on oral departure reasons, but nine judges (author plus eight concurring) sat, i.e. the court en banc; bench limb fails.

citing_name: Singleton v. United Servs. Auto. Ass'n
citing_court: Court of Appeal of Louisiana, Fifth Circuit
cited_name: Silva v. State Farm Mutual Automobile Insurance Co.
explanation: Fifth Circuit specifically overruled Silva, but grounded it on earlier Louisiana Supreme Court authority (Ortego) that Silva ignored; no judges line given, and from my recollection the case was heard en banc. Exception limb fails.
Commonwealth Court overruled Acton, Luckey and Browne, but sat as a seven-judge en banc court and relied on Supreme Court decisions O'Connell, McFadden and intervening Mihalaki; bench limb fails.

citing_name: Progressive Classic Insurance Co. v. Nationwide Mutual Fire Insurance
cited_name: Dairyland Insurance v. State Farm Automobile Insurance
explanation: Georgia Court of Appeals disapproved Dairyland's 'other insurance' language, but all twelve judges participated (whole court), and the language was arguably dicta contrary to earlier cases; bench limb fails.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit
cited_name: Biscayne Trust Co. v. American Security & Trust Co.
explanation: Three-judge division (2-1) declared Caffrey, Biscayne and Lockwood 'should be overruled' as misunderstanding earlier cases; dissent says they were express holdings; no intervening authority. From knowledge: D.C. Circuit sat en banc by 1948, though its prior-panel rule was then less firm.

Second DCA panel receded only from 'statements' on prior notice; Kroenke's holding concerned the missing hearing on amount (notice was given there), so the statement was dictum and Kroenke's holding is untouched; departs limb fails.
First Circuit overruled Hudson v. Day, but thirteen judges sat (en banc) and the court relied on the intervening Supreme Court ruling in State v. Mayer; bench limb fails.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit
explanation: Rhodes panel expressly overruled Copelin's sua sponte limiting-instruction rule, but the footnote states the overruling was circulated to and approved by the full court (Irons v. Diamond procedure), also resting on Fed. R. Evid. 105; limb 3 fails.

Buss expressly overruled Riley (and Slack) in a footnote, but it was decided by seven judges of the Commonwealth Court sitting en banc (President Judge Craig and six judges), not a three-judge panel; limb 2 fails.

citing_name: Ionics, Inc. v. Elmwood Sensors, Inc.
citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the First Circuit
cited_name: Roto-Lith, Ltd. v. F. P. Bartlett & Co.
explanation: Ionics panel overruled Roto-Lith, but footnote says departure was compelled by the statute itself and the opinion was circulated to all active judges, none of whom objected; recognised First Circuit informal en banc circulation, so limb 3 fails.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit
explanation: Ortiz panel overruled Collado's reading of 21 U.S.C. 851(a)(2), but footnote states the opinion was circulated before filing to all active judges with no objection (Second Circuit mini en banc); limb 3 fails.

citing_name: Fidelity & Casualty Co. of New York v. De Jesus
cited_name: Werner v. Safeco Insurance Co. of America
explanation: De Jesus (3d DCA panel) receded from American Service Mutual v. Wilson, not the named Werner decision, a Fourth DCA per curiam sharing page 645; different case and district. It also relied on earlier Florida Supreme Court authority (Rutkin). Limb 1 fails.

Hobbs expressly overruled Collier v. Marsh and Jones v. Cropps in part, but eight judges participated (author plus seven concurring, one not participating), i.e. the whole nine-judge Georgia Court of Appeals as then constituted, not a three-judge division; limb 2 fails.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit
explanation: LaFountain panel overruled McGore's no-leave-to-amend rule, but expressly because McGore is flatly inconsistent with the intervening Supreme Court decision in Jones v. Bock (2007); recognised intervening higher-court ground, so limb 3 fails.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
explanation: Three-judge panel overruled Caldwell's per se prejudice holding, but expressly because it is clearly irreconcilable with the intervening Supreme Court decision in Neder, invoking Miller v. Gammie; limb 3 fails.

citing_name: Nobelpharma AB v. Implant Innovations, Inc.
citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit
cited_name: Atari, Inc. v. JS & A Group, Inc.
explanation: Panel opinion expressly overruled Atari, Loctite and Cygnus on choice of circuit law, but footnote states that section was considered and decided unanimously by the in banc court; limbs 2 and 3 fail.

Second District panel receded from O'Brien and Solis, but grounded this on conflict with the earlier Florida Supreme Court decision in Bell; also, from my knowledge, Florida DCAs had no en banc procedure until 1980; limbs 3 and 4 fail.
Louisiana First Circuit overruled Harris and Miceli to the extent of conflict, but the judges line lists thirteen judges with multiple concurrences and dissents, an en banc sitting; limb 2 fails.

citing_name: Jubber v. SMC Electrical Products, Inc.
citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit
explanation: Panel overruled Jobin and Fidelity Savings on the standard of review, but the footnote states the opinion was circulated to all unrecused active judges and all agreed; full-court approval means limb 3 fails.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit
explanation: Panel abrogated Hall's uniform remand rule in Anders cases, but acknowledged the prior-panel rule and stated the opinion was circulated to all active members of the court; limb 3 fails.

citing_name: United States Steel Corp. v. Unemployment Compensation Board of Review
cited_name: Ehman v. Unemployment Compensation Board of Review
explanation: Commonwealth Court sat as seven judges including the President Judge, an en banc bench, when departing from Ehman (overruling passage omitted from excerpt; relying on my knowledge and the dissent); limb 2 fails.

citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit
cited_name: Inland Steel Co. v. LTV Steel Co.
explanation: Raniere panel cites Inland Steel as its Buckhannon reading and does not overrule it; any shift from a merits requirement rests expressly on the intervening Supreme Court decision in CRST, a recognised ground.

Three-justice Beaumont panel expressly overruled its own Jackson to the extent of conflict, citing only that section 5(b) was not argued there; no higher-court, en banc or statutory-change ground relied on. Prior-panel rule and TRAP 41.2 en banc from own knowledge.

citing_name: McCann v. Texas City Refining, Inc.
citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit
cited_name: Burns v. Texas City Refining, Inc.
explanation: Fifth Circuit panel 'disapproved' any Burns language suggesting prejudgment interest alongside liquidated damages, but framed it as clarifying imprecise wording; Burns's actual holding on backpay interest is not in the text given, so departure from a holding cannot be settled.

citing_name: Florida Reinvestment Corp. v. Cypress Savings Ass'n
explanation: Fourth DCA receded from State ex rel. Guterma v. Douglas, not the named Second DCA Allstate v. Jackson (shared page cite); nine judges participated, so the receding was by the court en banc, not a panel.

citing_name: Chamber of Commerce of the United States v. Lockyer
citing_court: United States Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit
cited_name: Associated Builders & Contractors, Inc. v. City of Seward
explanation: Ninth Circuit panel merely cited Seward as an example of the market participant exception applying and distinguished the California statute as regulatory; it did not overrule, disapprove or refuse to follow Seward.
